chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn from Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjāl from some of his men from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That Allah the Exalted made the Ka'bah the qiblah for the people of the Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram), and made the Mosque the qiblah for the people of the Sanctuary (al-Haram), and made the Sanctuary the qiblah for the people of the world.

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (the sacred precincts surrounding the mosque)
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةُ: The Ka'bah, the cube-shaped building in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the hierarchical definition of the qiblah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* articulates a cosmological hierarchy of sacred space, reflecting the Shia understanding of concentric sanctity radiating from the Ka'bah. It establishes that the direction of prayer is relative to one's proximity to the holiest site, with the Ka'bah serving as the ultimate focal point for all humanity, thereby reinforcing the unity of the global Muslim community (*Ummah*) in worship.
